The SB 254/CSFA Senate Committee on Regulated Industries and Utilities offered Bill 254 By: Senator Cowsert of the following substitute to SB 254: 46th
AS PASSED SENATE A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT
To amend Chapter 23 of Title 2 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, the "Georgia Hemp Farming Act," so as to prohibit the sale of consumable hemp beverages that contain THC; to provide milligram limits on THC in consumable hemp products; to provide for a definition; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF GEORGIA:
SECTION … paragraph to read as follows: "(28.1) 'Total THC' means delta-8-tetrahydrocannabinol, delta-9-THC, delta-10-tetrahydrocannabinol, or any combination thereof."
SECTION 2. Said chapter is further amended by revising Code Section 2-23-9.2, relating to consumable hemp products, packaging, advertising, and distribution, as follows: SB 254/CSFA
"2-23-9.2. (a) No consumable hemp product shall be sold or otherwise distributed in this state unless such product is packaged in a container that: (1) Is not attractive to children; (2) Does not bear any reasonable resemblance to any … term shall not include gummies, consumable base oils, or products that constitute drinks or beverages. (B) 'Gummy' means a gelatinous substance in the form of a cube, sphere, prismatoid, ovoid, or other shape that is designed for human ingestion.
SB 254/CSFA (2) No consumable hemp product shall be sold or otherwise distributed in this state if such product constitutes or is a component of: (A) A food product; or (B) A drink or beverage that that: (i) Contains contains alcohol or constitutes an alcoholic beverage under Title 3. 3; or (ii) Contains THC. (3) Nothing in this subsection is intended to prohibit the sale or distribution of hemp that is contained within gummies or consumable base oils, provided that such gummies or consumable base oils are not a component of a food product. product or a drink or beverage. (d)(1) Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (2), (3), (2) and (4) (3) of this subsection, no consumable hemp product shall be sold or otherwise distributed in this state if such product has more than: (A) Ten milligrams of total THC per serving; or (B) 150 milligrams of total THC per container. (2) No consumable hemp product that constitutes a drink or beverage shall be sold or otherwise distributed in this state if such product: (A) Has more than five milligrams of total THC per 12 fluid ounces of liquid, or the proportionate equivalent thereof; or (B) Is packaged in a container that exceeds 12 fluid ounces of liquid. (3) No consumable hemp product that is intended for topical application shall be sold or otherwise distributed in this state if such product is packaged in a container that has more than 1,000 milligrams of total THC. (4) (3) No consumable hemp product that constitutes a tincture shall be sold or otherwise distributed in this state if such product: (A) Has more than one milligram of total THC per one milliliter of liquid, or the proportionate equivalent thereof; or (B) Is packaged in a container that exceeds 60 milliliters of liquid."
SECTION 3. All laws and parts of laws in conflict with this Act are repealed.
